title_en: Population and Family Planning Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution for the purposes of achieving coordinated development of population with economy, society, resources and the environment, promoting family planning, protecting the legitimate rights and interests of citizens, and facilitating family well-being, national prosperity and social progress.

Article 2 China is a country with a large population, and implementing family planning is a basic State policy of the country.
The State takes comprehensive measures to regulate the population size, improve population quality, promote the realization of an appropriate fertility level, optimize the population structure, and facilitate the long-term balanced development of population.
The State shall, by relying on publicity and education, scientific and technological progress, comprehensive services, establishment and improvement of the reward and social security system, carry out the work of population and family planning.
Article 3 The work of population and family planning shall be combined with increasing women's opportunities for education and employment, improving women's health and raising women's status.

Article 4 People's governments at all levels and their staff members shall strictly administer according to law, enforce the law with civility, and shall not infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of citizens in the implementation of family planning.
The health and health commission departments and their staff members, when performing their official duties according to law, shall be protected by law.

Article 5 The State Council shall lead the work of population and family planning throughout the country.
Local people's governments at all levels shall lead the work of population and family planning within their respective administrative areas.

Article 6 The health and health commission department of the State Council shall be responsible for the nationwide family planning work and the population work related to family planning.
The health and health commission departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the family planning work and the population work related to family planning within their respective administrative areas.
Other relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall, within the scope of their respective responsibilities, be responsible for the relevant work of population and family planning.

Article 7 Trade unions, the Communist Youth League, women's federations, family planning associations and other social organizations, enterprises, institutions and citizens shall assist the people's governments in carrying out the work of population and family planning.
Article 8 The State shall give awards to organizations and individuals that have made outstanding achievements in the work of population and family planning.

Article 9 The State Council shall formulate population development plans and incorporate them into the national economic and social development plans.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the national population development plan and the population development plan of the government at the next higher level and in light of the local actual conditions, formulate population development plans for their respective administrative areas and incorporate them into the national economic and social development plans.

Article 10 People's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the population development plans, formulate implementation plans for population and family planning and organize their implementation.
The health and health commission departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the daily work of implementing the implementation plans for population and family planning.
People's governments of townships, nationality townships and towns and the sub-district offices of cities shall be responsible for the work of population and family planning within their respective jurisdictions and shall implement the implementation plans for population and family planning.

Article 11 The implementation plan for population and family planning shall prescribe measures for regulating the population size, improving population quality, promoting the realization of an appropriate fertility level, optimizing the population structure, strengthening maternal and infant health care and infant and toddler care services, and facilitating family development.

Article 12 Villagers' committees and residents' committees shall, according to law, do a good job in family planning work.
State organs, armed forces, social organizations, enterprises and institutions shall do a good job in family planning work of their own units.

Article 13 The departments of health and health commission, education, science and technology, culture, civil affairs, press and publication, radio and television, etc. shall organize publicity and education on population and family planning.
The mass media shall have the obligation to carry out public welfare publicity on population and family planning.
Schools shall, in a manner appropriate to the characteristics of the educatees and in a planned way, carry out education on physiological health, adolescence education or sexual health education among students.

Article 14 The family planning work for the floating population shall be jointly managed by the people's governments of their places of household registration and their current places of residence, with the current place of residence as the main responsible party.

Article 15 The State shall gradually increase the overall level of investment in population and family planning funds in accordance with the national economic and social development. People's governments at all levels shall ensure the necessary funds for the work of population and family planning.
People's governments at all levels shall give priority support to the work of population and family planning in underdeveloped areas and ethnic minority areas.
The State encourages social organizations, enterprises, institutions and individuals to make donations for the work of population and family planning.
No unit or individual may intercept, deduct, misappropriate or divert the funds for the work of population and family planning.
Article 16 The State encourages scientific research and international exchanges and cooperation in the field of population and family planning.

Article 17 Citizens have the right to bear children and also have the obligation to practice family planning according to law. Both husband and wife share the joint responsibility in practicing family planning.

Article 18 The State advocates marriage and childbearing at appropriate ages, and eugenics and better child rearing. A married couple may have three children.
Where the conditions prescribed by laws and regulations are met, a couple may request to have additional children. The specific measures shall be prescribed by the people's congresses or their standing committees of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government.
Ethnic minorities also shall practice family planning, and the specific measures shall be prescribed by the people's congresses or their standing committees of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government.
Where the provisions on having additional children differ between the provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government where the spouses have their household registration, the principle favorable to the parties shall apply.

Article 19 The State shall create conditions to ensure that citizens can make informed choices of safe, effective and appropriate contraceptive measures. The implementation of contraceptive operations shall ensure the safety of the persons receiving the operations.
Article 20 Couples of childbearing age shall independently choose contraceptive measures for family planning to prevent and reduce unintended pregnancies.

Article 21 Couples of childbearing age who practice family planning shall be entitled to free family planning technical services for basic items prescribed by the State.
The expenses required for the preceding paragraph shall be included in the fiscal budget or be ensured by social insurance in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 22 Discrimination against or maltreatment of women who give birth to female babies or women who are infertile is prohibited.
Discrimination against, maltreatment of or abandonment of female babies is prohibited.
Article 23 The State shall, in accordance with the provisions, give awards to couples who practice family planning.

Article 24 The State shall establish and improve social security systems such as basic old-age insurance, basic medical insurance, maternity insurance and social welfare to promote family planning.
The State encourages insurance companies to offer insurance programs conducive to family planning.

Article 25 Couples who give birth to children in accordance with laws and regulations may obtain extended maternity leave awards or other welfare benefits.
The State supports local governments with the conditions to establish parental leave.

Article 26 During pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding, women shall enjoy special labor protection according to the relevant provisions of the State and may receive assistance and compensation. The State protects the legitimate rights and interests of women in employment and provides employment services to women whose employment is affected by childbirth.
Citizens who undergo family planning operations shall enjoy the leave provided by the State.
Article 27 The State shall adopt support measures in fiscal, tax, insurance, education, housing, employment, etc. to reduce the burden of childbirth, child-rearing and education on families.

Article 28 People's governments at or above the county level shall comprehensively take measures such as planning, land, housing, fiscal, financial and talent measures to promote the establishment of an inclusive childcare service system and improve the accessibility and fairness of services for families with infants and toddlers.
The State encourages and guides social forces to establish childcare institutions, and supports kindergartens, government organs, enterprises, institutions and communities to provide childcare services.
The establishment and services of childcare institutions shall comply with the relevant standards and norms of childcare services. Childcare institutions shall register with the health and health commission departments of the people's governments at the county level.

Article 29 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in the construction and renovation of urban and rural communities, build activity venues and supporting service facilities for infants and toddlers that are commensurate with the scale of the permanent resident population.
Public places and employers with a relatively large number of female employees shall set up maternal and infant facilities to provide convenience for infant and toddler care and breastfeeding.

Article 30 People's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen support and guidance for family infant and toddler care, and enhance families' scientific child-rearing ability.
Medical and health institutions shall, in accordance with the provisions, carry out services such as vaccination, disease prevention and control for families with infants and toddlers, and provide health guidance on dietary nutrition, growth and development, etc.

Article 31 During the period when the State advocates that a couple shall have only one child, couples who voluntarily have only one child throughout their lives shall be issued the Certificate of Honor for the Parents with One Child by the State.
Couples who have obtained the Certificate of Honor for the Parents with One Child shall enjoy the rewards for parents with one child in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and the provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government.
Where measures for rewards given to couples who have obtained the Certificate of Honor for the Parents with One Child are prescribed by laws, regulations or rules and are to be implemented by the units where the couples work, the relevant units shall implement them.
During the period when the State advocates that a couple shall have only one child, those who, according to the provisions, shall enjoy the reward and assistance for the elderly of family planning families shall continue to enjoy the relevant reward and assistance, and shall be given necessary priority and care in terms of welfare for the elderly and elderly care services.

Article 32 Couples who have obtained the Certificate of Honor for the Parents with One Child shall, in the event of accidental disability or death of their only child, receive assistance in accordance with the provisions. People's governments at or above the county level shall establish and improve comprehensive support and security systems for the above-mentioned groups in terms of living, elderly care, medical care, spiritual consolation, etc.

Article 33 Local people's governments at all levels shall provide support and preferential treatment in terms of funds, technology, training, etc. to families in rural areas that practice family planning for their economic development; and shall give priority care to poor families that practice family planning in terms of poverty alleviation loans, work-for-relief projects, poverty alleviation projects and social relief.

Article 34 For the reward and social security measures prescribed in this Chapter, the people's congresses and their standing committees or the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and of cities divided into districts and autonomous prefectures may, in accordance with this Law and the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations, and in light of the local actual conditions, formulate specific implementation measures.
Article 35 The State shall establish a premarital health care system and a maternity care system to prevent or reduce birth defects and improve the health level of newborn babies.
Article 36 People's governments at all levels shall take measures to ensure that citizens enjoy family planning services and improve citizens' reproductive health level.

Article 37 Medical and health institutions shall carry out publicity and education on eugenics and better child rearing for people of childbearing age, provide periconceptional and maternity care services for women of childbearing age, undertake consultation, guidance and technical services on family planning, eugenics and better child rearing, and reproductive health care, and standardize the diagnosis and treatment of infertility.

Article 38 Family planning technical service personnel shall guide citizens who practice family planning to choose safe, effective and appropriate contraceptive measures.
The State encourages the research, application and promotion of new technologies and new drugs and devices for family planning.

Article 39 The use of ultrasound technology and other technical means for non-medical fetal sex identification is strictly prohibited; the non-medical selective termination of pregnancy by gender is strictly prohibited.

Article 41 Where a childcare institution violates the relevant standards and norms for childcare services, the health and health commission department shall order it to make corrections and give it a warning; if it refuses to make corrections, a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the childcare service shall be ordered to cease, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed.
Where a childcare institution has acted to abuse infants or toddlers, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be prohibited from engaging in infant and toddler care services for life; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 42 Where a family planning technical service person violates operational procedures or delays rescue, diagnosis or treatment, causing serious consequences, the corresponding legal liability shall be assumed in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 44 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a party fails to perform the obligation of assisting in family planning management, the relevant local people's government shall order it to make corrections and circulate a notice of criticism; the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given a disciplinary sanction according to law.

Article 45 Anyone who refuses or obstructs the health and health commission department and its staff members from performing their official duties according to law shall be given criticism and education by the health and health commission department and be stopped; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, a public security administrative penalty shall be imposed according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 46 Where a citizen, legal person or other organization considers that an administrative organ has infringed upon its lawful rights and interests in the process of implementing family planning management, it may apply for administrative reconsideration or file an administrative action according to law.

Article 47 The specific measures for the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the Chinese People's Armed Police Force to implement this Law shall be formulated by the Central Military Commission in accordance with this Law.
Article 48 This Law shall come into force as of September 1, 2002.
